name: Radial Tunnel Syndrome
definition: Painful radial-tunnel compression syndrome causing proximal dorsal forearm pain, usually without major objective motor loss.

investigations.principle: Primarily clinical; electrodiagnostics may be normal and imaging is cause-directed.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, postoperative, infection, occult injury or condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific pathway.

amber: Persistent focal symptoms may require decompression.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Bahu/Vata-neuralgic phenotype may be documented only in parallel.

patientEducation.summary: Painful radial-tunnel compression syndrome causing proximal dorsal forearm pain, usually without major objective motor loss.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for progressive neurological deficit, sphincter change, major trauma, unstable fracture/dislocation, sepsis/infection or other listed red flags.
